doc.title: Johnny Varro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

title: Keeping a book instead of a band
summary: He keeps his book and picks up local players in New York, Florida and Los Angeles.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Is it conceivable to keep a band together these days as a working unit?
Well I don’t keep a band together because it’s hard to keep them. You know I keep my book together.

Wherever I go if I’m in New York I pick up the New York players, which is usually the guys that are on the CDs. In Florida here I have a Florida band, and when I go out to L.A. © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-

I pick up a bunch of guys from L.A. So as long as the book is together, and these guys can all play here, there, everywhere, as long as they can read and have a sense of improvisation, the band is usually good. But the New York boys are —
I guess there’s a reason for that. Everybody seems to end up there at least for part of their careers.
Well look at the personnel, my God. You know these are the top players.
